_style: Address the user with respectful plural «تاسو» (ستاسو، تاسو ته، imperatives in ـئ: «وګورئ»، «ولیکئ»), which is gender-neutral; address the couple as «تاسو دواړه» and refer to them together as «تاسو دواړه» / «یوځای». The other person is «ستاسو ملګری» (life partner, used as a grammatically masculine generic noun like Spanish “pareja”); never use مېړه/ښځه/نامزد/محبوب/محبوبه. Pashto marks gender in past-tense verbs and adjectives, so avoid sentences that make the user or partner the subject of a gendered past participle or adjective: prefer present/future tense, verbal nouns and passive or impersonal phrasing («نوی پیغام له %@ څخه» not «%@ ولېږه/ولېږله»; «پیل کوو؟» not «چمتو یاست؟»), or reword around the name or «تاسو دواړه». Short in-app messages that one partner sends to the other (reactions, pings) may use intimate singular imperative («زنګ راته ووهه»). A partner's name placeholder %@ is never inflected or given case endings or suffixes; use it with prepositions/postpositions («د %@ لپاره»، «له %@ سره»، «%@ ته») or rephrase. Quotes: guillemets « » as outer marks only where English has quotes, inner ‹ ›; punctuation is Pashto/Arabic: comma ، semicolon ؛ question mark ؟ period . and ellipsis … as one character, no space before punctuation, keep “ · ” separators, \n and emoji exactly. Keep every placeholder (%@, %lld, %1$@…) and never write numbers as literal digits in place of a placeholder; numbers and dates are formatted by the system (Gregorian calendar, the locale may show ۰۱۲۳ digits); if a literal digit is unavoidable, use Extended Arabic-Indic digits ۰–۹. Buttons and actions are short verbal nouns (infinitives) or iOS-style nouns with no final period: «ساتل»، «لغوه»، «بشپړ»، «لېږل»، «بیا هڅه»؛ titles, tabs and headers are short noun phrases with no period. Pashto has no capitalization; keep Coupley, Premium, CoupleSync and AI in Latin script and let bidi handle them (no manual RLM/LRM unless a line starts with Latin or a placeholder and renders wrongly). Script: use Pashto letters ټ ډ ړ ږ ښ ځ څ ڼ ګ (U+06AB, not گ) and Persian ک (U+06A9, not ك); distinguish ی / ي / ې / ۍ / ئ correctly; standard written Pashto, avoid heavy Persian or English loans where a common Pashto word exists. Plural categories are ["one","other"]: «one» uses the singular noun («%lld ورځ»), «other» the plural («%lld ورځې»). Tone: warm, kind, light, natural Pashto of a good app — never literal, never syrupy.
